summary:
Project Summary 

Project Name / Idea: SI-Powered Space Fire Safety Dashboard & Early Warning System.

Project Overview:
As humanity prepares to return to the Moon and press on to Mars, spacecraft fire safety is more critical than ever. Due to the overwhelming and scattered volume of decades of NASA microgravity combustion data within the Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database, our team has built a centralized, all-in-one smart platform.

Key Features & Core Technologies:

 * Unified Data Hub: Aggregates and organizes all microgravity combustion experiments (such as BASS, Saffire, FLEX, and ACME) into a single, highly searchable, and comparable interface.

 * AI & Super Intelligence (SI) Tool: Automatically summarizes, ranks, and interprets complex scientific data, helping engineers and researchers build predictive flammability models for high-oxygen exploration environments (like lunar bases and rovers).

 * Smart Early Warning Alarm System: An advanced hazard detection mechanism specifically engineered for space habitats to identify smoke, invisible cool flames, and potential fire threats at their earliest stages—protecting astronauts hundreds of thousands of miles away from home.
details:
Project Details

* What does it do or how does it work?

The project is a centralized, AI- and Super Intelligence (SI)-powered dashboard that aggregates decades of NASA microgravity combustion research (from the PSI database) into a single, unified platform. It uses intelligent algorithms to automatically summarize, rank, and interpret experimental data. Furthermore, it integrates a smart early warning fire alarm system that detects smoke and invisible hazards (such as cool flames) to alert astronauts before a threat escalates.

* What benefits does it have?

* Eliminates data overload and drastically reduces the time engineers and researchers spend searching through scattered reports.

* Streamlines the material selection and safety compliance process for spacecraft design.

* Bridges raw scientific experimentation with practical, mission-critical engineering solutions.

* What is the intended impact of the project?

To significantly enhance astronaut safety during deep space exploration missions to the Moon and Mars, safeguard critical habitats against extreme fire hazards, and derive spin-off safety benefits for terrestrial applications on Earth.

* What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

* Programming & Core: Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS.

* AI & Data Processing: Machine learning and Natural Language Processing (NLP) frameworks for parsing and indexing PSI combustion datasets.

* Design & Prototyping: Canva, PowerPoint, and Gamma for crafting interactive 3D UI layouts and project presentations.

* How is your project creative?

Our project creatively transforms overwhelming, heterogeneous scientific archives into an interactive "decision-making engine." It uniquely predicts flammability behaviors under extreme lunar habitat conditions (high oxygen environments ≥ 30% O₂) and introduces proactive microgravity-tailored hazard detection.

* What factors did your team consider?

* The unique atmospheric constraints of upcoming lunar bases and pressurized rovers (low pressure combined with elevated oxygen concentration).

* Compatibility with shared International Space Station hardware test rigs (e.g., CIR and MSG).

* Accessibility and user experience for a diverse audience, ranging from aerospace researchers to university students.
dataRefs: NASA ScienceCasts: The Power of Studying Combustion on the ISS
